title: Urban growth is not yet producing adequate housing, public space, transport access, or resilient services at scale
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division, Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026, Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities
geography: Global urban settlements, housing, informal settlements, land use, public space, transport, disaster resilience, and urban governance

denominator.unit: global urban population and housing-condition frame

slum_population.unit: millions of urban residents living in slums or informal settlements in 2024

slum_share.value: almost one in four urban residents

service_deficit.value: many residents lack safe water, sanitation, secure housing, or adequate living space

observations.method: UN SDG compilation of global urban housing, informal-settlement, service, and living-condition indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Global slum and informal-settlement estimates depend on definitions, enumeration, and country reporting; the aggregate does not measure individual housing histories, tenure security, or resident preferences.
observations.subgroup: Urban residents in informal settlements, renters, displaced people, low-income households, women, children, migrants, and people exposed to environmental hazards.
observations.counterinterpretation: Informal settlements can provide access to jobs, social networks, and affordable urban entry even while residents face serious service, legal, and safety deficits.

observations.period: 2020-2025; public space and urban land allocation

denominator.unit: cities in 126 countries with comparable public-space and urban-land data

streets_open_space_2020.unit: percent of urban land allocated to streets and open spaces in 2020

streets_open_space_2025.unit: percent of urban land allocated to streets and open spaces in 2025

target_gap.value: the increase remains far below the recommended 30 to 45 percent range

observations.method: UN SDG analysis of city-level land allocation, public space, and urban form indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The city sample is not all cities and land-allocation measures do not establish accessibility, safety, quality, or equitable use of public space.
observations.subgroup: Pedestrians, children, older adults, people with disabilities, low-income residents, street vendors, commuters, and communities lacking accessible public space.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small aggregate land-share change can coexist with meaningful local improvements, while a higher share can still be poorly located, inaccessible, or unsafe.

denominator.unit: urban transport, public-service access, disaster-risk, and opportunity frame

transport_channel.value: access to public transport shapes economic prospects and quality of life for city residents

service_resilience.value: cities face risks from disasters, critical-infrastructure disruption, and basic-service interruption

opportunity_link.value: housing location, transport, services, and public space jointly condition access to work, health, education, and social life

observations.method: UN SDG comparative review of transport, resilience, infrastructure, public-space, and urban-service indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies system linkages but does not estimate individual commute effects, causal housing-to-opportunity pathways, or city-specific resilience outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Transit-dependent residents, workers, students, caregivers, people with disabilities, peripheral neighborhoods, and communities exposed to disasters or service outages.
observations.counterinterpretation: Walking, cycling, informal transport, remote work, and local service provision can offset some formal transport deficits, though they may not be safe, reliable, or equally available.

observations.period: 2026; urban data, participation, and local implementation

denominator.unit: city and neighborhood data, local governance, participation, and SDG implementation frame

data_gap.value: urban data remain insufficiently disaggregated to understand inequalities affecting vulnerable people and neighborhoods

local_delivery.value: housing, transport, public space, climate resilience, and services depend on local planning, finance, maintenance, and participation

policy_question.value: the open question is whether urban growth creates shared access and voice or reproduces spatial exclusion

observations.method: UN SDG synthesis of urban indicators and data limitations connected to local implementation and governance.
observations.uncertainty: This is a cross-source analytical bridge, not a causal estimate from the SDG report; data gaps may conceal both progress and exclusion.
observations.subgroup: Municipal governments, neighborhood organizations, informal-settlement residents, planners, service providers, developers, and groups underrepresented in city data.
observations.counterinterpretation: Participatory upgrading, better local data, and community-led planning can improve delivery without requiring uniform national policy or formal tenure first.

related_sources.claim: UN-Habitat World Cities Report 2026 provides complementary narrative analysis of the global housing crisis, displacement, and urban resilience.
UN DESA World Urbanization Prospects 2025 provides complementary population distribution and urbanization projections.

boundary: This record adds a global urban housing, informal-settlement, public-space, transport, resilience, data, and local-governance route. It uses aggregate SDG indicators and city comparisons, not individual housing histories, respondent-level resident sentiment, causal commute or health estimates, or proof that urban investment produces equitable access.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN SDG 2026 Goal 11 materials were reviewed for urban informal settlements, public-space land allocation, transport and opportunity, service resilience, and urban data gaps.
